# vibld's MCP server

docs/decisions.md D182. An assistant a person connects to vibld (Claude,
Cursor, any MCP client) can find a template, start a build, follow it and
open its preview, on that person's own account: their plan, their credit,
their projects. Since D190 it can also edit a project's code itself: read
and write its files, type-check them, take screenshots of its preview, and
go back to a checkpoint, with no build and no credit spent, within a daily
number of calls set by the plan (D201).

## How it works

- **Endpoint:** `https://app.vibld.com/mcp`, served by the builder's own
  Worker (`apps/web/worker/mcp-server.ts`). MCP Streamable HTTP, stateless:
  each JSON-RPC message is one POST answered with one JSON body. No session
  is kept and the server sends nothing unasked, so `GET` and `DELETE` answer 405.
- **Sign-in:** OAuth 2.1, with Clerk (`https://clerk.vibld.com`) as the
  authorization server. A client with no token is answered 401 with a
  `WWW-Authenticate` header naming
  `https://app.vibld.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp` (RFC
  9728), which names Clerk. The person signs in to vibld as they always do
  and approves the assistant. Nothing here creates accounts: D180 stands.
- **Discovery before sign-in (D222):** that 401, for an `initialize` or a
  `tools/list` with no token at all, carries the JSON-RPC answer in its
  body: the server's instructions and the full tool list. The status and
  challenge are unchanged, so a client still signs the person in; a
  directory or scanner can read what vibld does. A tool call, any other
  method, or an invalid token gets the plain 401.
- **Connecting:** https://vibld.com/docs/assistants, with an "Add to
  Claude" link (D220) that opens Claude's connector dialog with this
  server filled in. The builder's settings menu has the same link.
- **Token check:** every token is checked with Clerk's Backend API
  (`mcp-auth.ts`), which says whether the person revoked it. Only opaque
  tokens are accepted, since a JWT access token cannot be revoked. A token Clerk vouched for is trusted for
  60 seconds, or until it expires if sooner. Its audience must name
  `https://app.vibld.com/mcp` (the RFC 8707 resource the client signs in
  for), and it must carry the `build` scope: a token from signing in
  to some other app with vibld (`openid`, `profile`) is answered 403
  `insufficient_scope`.
- **Two scopes:** `build` connects, and is all the five original tools
  need. The editing tools, `take_screenshot` among them, need `edit` as
  well (Chris, 2026-10-11). A call to one on a token without it is
  answered with the MCP authorization spec's step-up (2025-11-25, "Scope
  Challenge Handling"): HTTP 403 with
  `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope", scope="build edit"`,
  before the call is counted or anything is read, so the client signs the
  person in again asking for both. Its JSON-RPC error says to connect vibld
  again and approve editing, for a client that does not step up. The 401
  that starts a connection asks for `build edit`, since some clients
  (claude.ai) ask for what it names and never follow the step-up, which
  left every editing tool refused. So the Clerk instance needs both scopes
  created (a Dashboard step, noted in `scripts/configure-accounts.mjs`),
  and every client registered before `edit` existed given it too, since
  Clerk answers a client asking for more than it registered with
  `invalid_scope` (`configure-accounts` does this on `apply`). The person
  still approves each scope. The protected resource metadata lists both in
  `scopes_supported`.
- **One door per token:** a Clerk session token does not open `/mcp`, and
  an OAuth token does not open the builder's `/api/*`. The builder's routes
  now refuse any Clerk-signed token without a session id (`principal.ts`),
  which is what OAuth access tokens and ID tokens lack.
- **The tools use the builder's own routes.** Each tool calls `/api/plan`,
  `/api/projects`, `/api/projects/:id/files`, `/api/projects/:id/checkpoints`,
  `/api/runs`, `/api/runs/:id`, `/api/preview` and `/api/templates/brief`
  as the person (`actAs`), so a build or an edit from an
  assistant is gated, priced, limited and charged exactly as one from the
  builder. An assistant gets no model policy or admin rights that are keyed
  on a verified email: it acts with the plan alone. While vibld is
  invite-only, the gate admits an assistant to an account that already
  redeemed its invite in the builder; it never redeems one itself.
- **One preview per account.** `get_preview_url`, `check_types` and
  `take_screenshot` move
  the account's preview to the requested project (or stop and restart it),
  so neither reports another project's preview as this one's.
- **Edits are checkpoints.** `write_files` sends
  `PUT /api/projects/:id/files`, which merges the files onto the accepted
  code and accepts the result as a new revision, recorded in the history
  as an `edit` (run id `edit-...`). It names the revision it was made
  against, and is refused (`checkpoint-moved`, with the current revision)
  if the project has moved on, while a build runs, and in an archived
  project, as a restore is. The project it leaves is held to the limits a
  build's base is (50 files of its own, not counting the ones Vibld writes,
  and 160,000 characters), so it can still be built on.
- **Dry runs (D212).** `write_files` with `dryRun: true` sends the same
  `PUT` with `dryRun: true`, which runs every check above and writes
  nothing: no revision, no checkpoint. It answers with the draft and the
  base it was made against; the tool returns a unified line diff of each
  changed file and the draft's type check, run by moving the account's
  preview onto the draft. `check_types` and `get_preview_url` move it back.
- **Plugin:** `plugins/vibld` packages this server with two skills for
  Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, and the repository is their marketplace
  (D207). Install steps are in `plugins/vibld/README.md`.
- **Server Card:** `https://vibld.com/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json`
  (SEP-1649), a static file in `apps/marketing/public`.

## Tools

| Tool               | What it does                                                                                |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `search_templates` | The template catalog's closest designs to a description, with each one's page on vibld.com  |
| `list_projects`    | The person's projects, with their share links and published sites                           |
| `start_build`      | A build from a description, in a new project or an existing one, optionally from a template |
| `get_build_status` | Where a build is: running (and its phase), accepted, failed or stopped                      |
| `get_preview_url`  | Starts or reuses the account's live preview of a project's current code, and its URL        |

The editing tools (D190), each counted against the plan's daily calls:

| Tool                 | What it does                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `list_files`         | A project's current files, with their sizes and the revision they are at                                                                                             |
| `read_files`         | Up to 20 files' contents, from the current code or a checkpoint; at most 100,000 characters a call                                                                   |
| `write_files`        | Writes up to 20 files and deletes up to 20 from the revision read; the result is a new checkpoint. With `dryRun`, writes nothing and returns the diff and type check |
| `check_types`        | Starts or reuses the live preview of the current code and reports its type check                                                                                     |
| `list_checkpoints`   | The project's checkpoints, newest first, and which is current                                                                                                        |
| `restore_checkpoint` | Makes a checkpoint the current code again, from the revision the list showed                                                                                         |
| `get_logs`           | The preview's state and type check, if it serves this code, and how the recent builds ended                                                                          |
| `take_screenshot`    | Starts or reuses the live preview of the current code and returns one page of it as an image                                                                         |

`start_build` makes a new project unless it is given one, so an assistant
never builds over whatever the person last had open in the builder.

`read_files` returns at most 100,000 characters a call, and a project file
may hold up to 160,000. A file that does not fit beside the others in a
call is named in `omitted`, to read in another. One that does not fit even
alone, read first, comes back in parts: the part names `nextOffset`, and
the next call names the one path with `offset` set to it.

`take_screenshot` loads a page of the preview (`path`, default `/`) in
Cloudflare Browser Rendering (`worker/screenshot.ts`, the `BROWSER`
binding) at the builder's Desktop, Tablet or Phone width (1280, 768 or
390, D192), and answers with an MCP image content block. The browser opens
the preview's own URL, the one `/api/preview` gives the account, which
carries the preview's token; the page path must stay on that origin. Each
capture is bounded: 20 seconds to load, at most 5 more for the network to
go quiet, a full page cut at 8,000 pixels tall, an image over 1.5 MB taken
again as a JPEG, and the browser closed whatever happens. Where `BROWSER`
is not bound (a self-hosted copy under Docker) the tool is not listed.

`get_logs` reports only what vibld records. A running project's server
output, runtime errors and browser console are not captured, and the tool
says so rather than answering with nothing.

## Limits on top of the plan

The plan's allowance and the ledger are the real ceiling, as for every
build. An assistant can loop where a person clicks, so `/mcp` adds:

| Limit                                | Where                    | Value                                     |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| Builds started from assistants a day | `VIBLD_MCP_DAILY_BUILDS` | 20 per account                            |
| Builds started from assistants       | `MCP_BUILD_BURST`        | 2 a minute per account                    |
| Messages                             | `MCP_BURST`              | 60 a minute per account                   |
| Messages before sign-in is checked   | `MCP_IP_BURST`           | 600 a minute per address                  |
| Calls to the editing tools a day     | `MCP_DAILY_EDIT_CALLS`   | Free 50, Build 500, Ship 2000 per account |
| File edits, from anywhere            | `EDIT_BURST`             | 30 a minute per account                   |
| Screenshots                          | `SCREENSHOT_BURST`       | 6 a minute per account                    |

Each assistant build is recorded in `mcp_builds` (migration 0052) with the
OAuth client that started it.

The editing tools cost nothing to run and are not metered (D201): the
person's assistant pays for its own tokens. What bounds them is the daily
cap, by plan, which counts every call to one of the eight, a read as much
as a write, over the last 24 hours. Screenshots are the one exception to
"cost nothing": Browser Rendering bills browser time, which
`SCREENSHOT_BURST` bounds on top of the cap. It is in `worker/entitlement.ts`, and
an admin can change a plan's under **Plans** (D134; NULL in
`plan_limits.mcp_daily_edit_calls` keeps the code's). A call takes its
place in `mcp_calls` (migration 0054) once its arguments are checked and
before it reads anything, so a malformed call costs nothing and a refused
one has read nothing; only the window's rows are kept. The refusal names
the cap and says the builder is not affected, and the five tools above are
not counted.

## Setup (once)

In the Clerk Dashboard, OAuth applications, Settings tab:
https://dashboard.clerk.com/~/oauth-applications

- **Scopes tab:** create the scope `build` (description: "Start and follow
  builds on your vibld account") and the scope `edit` (description: "Read
  and edit the files of your vibld projects"), and turn on advertising both
  in Clerk's OAuth metadata.
- **Settings tab, Client onboarding:** Client ID Metadata Documents and
  Dynamic Client Registration both on (D185), and **Default scopes for
  dynamic clients** `openid profile email build edit`. Default scopes apply
  only when a client names none, so `scripts/configure-accounts.mjs` also
  caps what such a client may request (`dynamic_client_allowed_scopes`) at
  those five plus `offline_access`. Clerk refuses both settings while `edit`
  does not exist, so create it first; the script reports the refusal and
  leaves the rest as it was.
- **Settings tab:** turn on the `aud` claim from the RFC 8707 resource
  parameter (`aud_claim_enabled`); without it no token names this server
  and every assistant is refused.
- **Settings tab, Access token format:** opaque. `/mcp` refuses JWT
  access tokens, because Clerk cannot revoke one: it would keep working
  for a day after the person disconnects the assistant.

Then deploy the web Worker (`deploy-web-preview.yml`), which applies
migrations 0052 and 0054.

`/mcp` and its metadata exist only where the Worker signs in with Clerk and
has `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` (it checks every token with it), D1 and the project
bucket; anywhere else both answer 404.

## Phases

1. **Built.** The endpoint, sign-in, the five tools, the limits, the
   Server Card (D182). Then the editing tools, their `edit` scope and
   their daily cap by plan (D190, D201), and screenshots of the preview
   with Browser Rendering (Chris, 2026-10-11).
2. **Next.** Stop a build; follow-up changes in conversation; publishing,
   only with the person's explicit confirmation in the tool call; CORS for
   browser-based clients such as the MCP Inspector; a list of connected
   assistants in the builder's settings, with a link to revoke one; the
   DNS-AID `_mcp` record (owned by the AI readiness work).
3. **Later.** Listing in the MCP Registry and assistants' connector
   directories, and a page about it on vibld.com. From D190, still to
   come: runtime and browser console logs, which nothing captures yet.

name: Deploy sandbox service

# Manual only, like "Deploy web preview". Deploy this before apps/web
# whenever PREVIEW_INTERNAL_SECRET changes or apps/preview itself changes --
# apps/web's service binding to it only routes successfully once
# "vibld-preview" actually exists.
on:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: deploy-sandbox-service
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  deploy:
    name: Build and deploy @vibld/preview
    # Runs only in the private working repository. The public copy
    # (vibld/vibld) has none of the secrets or deployment environments this
    # job reads, so there it could only fail.
    if: github.repository == 'vibld/vibld-internal'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15

    # Same "preview" environment apps/web and apps/marketing already deploy
    # from -- see apps/preview/README.md for exactly which token scopes it
    # needs beyond what's already there (DNS: Edit on vibld-preview.dev).
    environment:
      name: preview

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Require Cloudflare credentials
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          PREVIEW_INTERNAL_SECRET: ${{ secrets.PREVIEW_INTERNAL_SECRET }}
        run: |
          missing=0
          [ -n "$CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" ] || { echo "::error::CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN is not set"; missing=1; }
          [ -n "$CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID" ] || { echo "::error::CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID is not set"; missing=1; }
          [ -n "$PREVIEW_INTERNAL_SECRET" ] || { echo "::error::PREVIEW_INTERNAL_SECRET is not set"; missing=1; }
          if [ "$missing" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "Add all three to the \"preview\" environment (Settings -> Environments)." >&2
            echo "The Cloudflare token needs \"Workers Scripts: Edit\" (already covers this account) and \"DNS: Edit\" on the vibld-preview.dev zone, for the wildcard route." >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      # The Sandbox SDK builds the container image at deploy time; GitHub's
      # ubuntu-24.04 runners ship Docker preinstalled, so this only ever
      # fails if that ever changes.
      - name: Require Docker
        run: docker info > /dev/null

      - name: Enable Corepack
        run: corepack enable

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Typecheck and test
        run: |
          pnpm --filter @vibld/preview typecheck
          pnpm --filter @vibld/preview test

      - name: Sync the internal secret to the Worker
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/preview
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          PREVIEW_INTERNAL_SECRET: ${{ secrets.PREVIEW_INTERNAL_SECRET }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The value goes in on stdin so it never appears in a command line
          # or in the run log.
          printf '%s' "$PREVIEW_INTERNAL_SECRET" | pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 secret put PREVIEW_INTERNAL_SECRET
          echo "Synced PREVIEW_INTERNAL_SECRET." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      # Signs and verifies share links (docs/decisions.md L10,
      # worker/share-token.ts). Optional, unlike PREVIEW_INTERNAL_SECRET
      # above: an unset value means /api/preview/share answers "not
      # configured" (a 503) rather than the whole deploy failing, the same
      # "additive, not load-bearing" rule PREVIEW_INTERNAL_SECRET itself
      # follows on apps/web's own deploy.
      - name: Sync the share secret to the Worker
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/preview
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          PREVIEW_SHARE_SECRET: ${{ secrets.PREVIEW_SHARE_SECRET }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -n "$PREVIEW_SHARE_SECRET" ]; then
            printf '%s' "$PREVIEW_SHARE_SECRET" | pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 secret put PREVIEW_SHARE_SECRET
            echo "Synced PREVIEW_SHARE_SECRET." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          else
            echo "PREVIEW_SHARE_SECRET not set -- /api/preview/share stays unconfigured on this deploy." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi

      # Building the container image can take several minutes on a cold
      # cache -- longer than apps/web's or apps/marketing's plain Worker
      # deploys, which upload source only.
      - name: Deploy to Cloudflare Workers
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/preview
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
        run: |
          pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 deploy
          echo "Deployed vibld-preview (*.vibld-preview.dev)" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

# Crux Consulting

A small management consultancy helping leadership teams make clear, accountable decisions.

A React, TypeScript and Vite project, styled with Tailwind CSS, with
shadcn/ui components, lucide-react icons and Motion for animation.

## Run it

You need Node.js 22 or later, with npm.

```bash
npm install
npm run dev
```

`npm run dev` starts a development server and prints the address to open.

## Build it

```bash
npm run build
```

This checks the types (`tsc --noEmit`) and then bundles the site into
`dist/`, which any static host can serve. `npm run preview` serves that
build locally.

## Scripts

| Script | Runs |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run dev` | `vite` |
| `npm run build` | `tsc --noEmit && vite build` |
| `npm run preview` | `vite preview` |
| `npm run lint` | `tsc --noEmit` |
| `npm run typecheck` | `tsc --noEmit` |

## Where things are

- `src/App.tsx`: the root component, which src/main.tsx renders.
- `src/pages/`: one file per page.
- `src/components/`: the page's sections and parts.
- `src/components/ui/`: shadcn/ui components, as source you can edit.
- `src/styles.css`: Tailwind CSS and the design's colors, fonts and spacing.
- `DESIGN.md`: the design this project is built to, with the exact values.

A browser-only recipe box. Save recipes with ingredients and numbered steps, search by name or ingredient, scale servings with quantities following, and mark favourites. All data is stored in your browser's localStorage and never leaves your device.

```bash
npm install
```

## Run

```bash
npm run dev
```

Open the local URL printed in the terminal (usually http://localhost:5173).


Produces a production build in the `dist` folder.

```bash
npm run typecheck
```

```bash
npm run lint
```

Runs TypeScript checks. No account or network service is required.

name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  quality:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    # vibld.com prerenders a page per gallery style (D143), 1,300+ pages,
    # which put the build past ten minutes on its own.
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Enable Corepack
        run: corepack enable

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        # Frozen: a lockfile that does not match package.json is a failure, not
        # something to paper over. The permissive install hid real drift --
        # packages/core was missing from the lockfile across four merges and
        # CI stayed green throughout.
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Format check
        run: pnpm format:check

      - name: House style
        run: pnpm check:style

      - name: Typecheck
        run: pnpm typecheck

      # vibld.com's tests build the site themselves and prerender a page per
      # gallery style (D143), each a request React Router fails after ten
      # seconds. Beside every other package's tests, on a runner's four
      # cores, a page took longer and the build failed (internal PR 356). So they run
      # on their own, after the rest.
      - name: Test
        run: pnpm test --filter='!@vibld/marketing'

      - name: Test vibld.com
        run: pnpm test --filter=@vibld/marketing

      # The repository scripts are not a workspace package, so turbo's test
      # task never reaches them. Their tests run here instead.
      - name: Script tests
        run: pnpm test:scripts

      # Every app's production build, which nothing above runs: typecheck
      # passes on code Vite then refuses to bundle, and until this step a
      # break like that reached main and was first seen by a deploy.
      #
      # The Clerk key is a placeholder. The build only embeds it, and a real
      # one would put an instance identifier in logs for no gain.
      #
      # Not vibld.com: its tests above ran its build script, postbuild
      # included, and a second prerender would only repeat it.
      - name: Build
        env:
          VITE_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY: pk_test_placeholder
        run: pnpm build --filter='!@vibld/marketing'

  # The eval stub reported a project accepted that stopped at
  # "vite: not found" (internal PR 59). Writing one case out and building it is the
  # only check that sees that. One case: they share a manifest, and each
  # build is a registry install. In a container, as the bakeoff runs
  # candidates, so the path a model's code takes is exercised on every pull
  # request.
  #
  # A job of its own, with its own time: one candidate may take up to 13
  # minutes at its worst (install, build, and the container's start and
  # removal), more than the quality job's limit allows after everything
  # else it runs (internal PR 237 review). The script is given what is left of the
  # job's time, less a reserve, so a slow registry is reported as a
  # candidate it had no time for, not cut off without a word.
  eval-build:
    name: Build what the eval stub accepts
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 25
    steps:
      - name: Note when the job started
        run: echo "JOB_STARTED=$(date +%s)" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Enable Corepack
        run: corepack enable

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      # Docker Hub refuses unauthenticated pulls past a limit that runners
      # share by address, which failed this job before any of it ran
      # (D187). Each Docker Hub image this job uses is pulled from
      # mirror.gcr.io and tagged with its Docker Hub name, so the build and
      # `docker run` find it locally and never ask Docker Hub. Setting the
      # daemon's `registry-mirrors` was tried first, and the pull still
      # went to Docker Hub.
      - name: Pull Docker Hub images through mirror.gcr.io
        run: |
          for image in node:24-bookworm-slim; do
            docker pull --quiet "mirror.gcr.io/library/$image"
            docker tag "mirror.gcr.io/library/$image" "docker.io/library/$image"
          done

      - name: Write one case out and build it
        run: |
          VIBLD_EVAL_OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/eval-stub" pnpm --filter @vibld/eval run eval --case coffee-roaster
          minutes=$(( (25 * 60 - ($(date +%s) - JOB_STARTED)) / 60 - 2 ))
          [ "$minutes" -ge 1 ] || minutes=1
          node --experimental-strip-types packages/eval/bin/build-candidates.ts "$RUNNER_TEMP/eval-stub" "$minutes" --container node:24-bookworm-slim

  # vibld under docker compose, with no Cloudflare account (D126): the
  # image builds, the three Workers start under workerd, and the owner
  # signs in. A preview's sandbox is a container on the runner's Docker
  # (D137); starting one is left to the end-to-end check (D122).
  docker:
    name: Docker
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 25
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24

      # Docker Hub refuses unauthenticated pulls past a limit that runners
      # share by address, which failed this job before any of it ran
      # (D187). Each Docker Hub image the Dockerfile and the VPS compose
      # file name is pulled from mirror.gcr.io and tagged with its Docker
      # Hub name, so the build and compose find it locally and never ask
      # Docker Hub. Setting the
      # daemon's `registry-mirrors` was tried first, and the pull still
      # went to Docker Hub.
      - name: Pull Docker Hub images through mirror.gcr.io
        run: |
          for image in docker:28-cli node:24-bookworm-slim traefik:v3; do
            docker pull --quiet "mirror.gcr.io/library/$image"
            docker tag "mirror.gcr.io/library/$image" "docker.io/library/$image"
          done

      - name: Start it
        env:
          # Not a secret: this copy lives for the length of the job.
          VIBLD_OWNER_PASSWORD: [REDACTED]
          # A local model (D124) with no server behind it: listing it needs
          # none, and building with it is not what this job checks.
          VIBLD_LOCAL_MODEL: ci-local-model
        run: |
          printf 'VIBLD_OWNER_PASSWORD=[REDACTED]' "$VIBLD_OWNER_PASSWORD" "$VIBLD_LOCAL_MODEL" > .env
          docker compose up --build --detach

      - name: Sign in
        env:
          VIBLD_OWNER_PASSWORD: [REDACTED]
          VIBLD_LOCAL_MODEL: ci-local-model
        run: node docker/smoke.mjs 900

      - name: Logs
        if: always()
        run: docker compose logs --no-color | tail -n 300

      # The same image as a container host runs it (D141, render.yaml): one
      # port from PORT, no Docker socket, the builder alone.
      - name: Start it on one port with the sandbox off
        env:
          VIBLD_OWNER_PASSWORD: [REDACTED]
        run: |
          docker compose down
          docker run --detach --name vibld-one-port -p 10000:10000 \
            -e VIBLD_SANDBOX=off -e PORT=10000 \
            -e VIBLD_OWNER_PASSWORD -e OPENAI_API_KEY=[REDACTED] \
            vibld

      - name: Sign in on one port
        env:
          VIBLD_OWNER_PASSWORD: [REDACTED]
          VIBLD_SANDBOX: 'off'
          PORT: '10000'
        run: node docker/smoke.mjs 600

      - name: Logs on one port
        if: always()
        run: docker logs vibld-one-port 2>&1 | tail -n 200 || true

      # As infrastructure/vps runs it on a server (D141): the proxy ends TLS
      # and the Workers listen on 127.0.0.1 only. The domains are made up,
      # so no certificate is issued and the proxy's own one is accepted.
      - name: Start it behind the server's proxy
        run: |
          docker rm --force vibld-one-port
          printf 'VIBLD_DOMAIN=build.vibld.test\nVIBLD_PREVIEW_DOMAIN=vibld-preview.test\nCF_DNS_API_TOKEN=[REDACTED]' >> .env
          docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f infrastructure/vps/compose.yml up --detach
          # The server's firewall rules apply, and applying them twice adds
          # nothing.
          sudo infrastructure/vps/firewall.sh
          sudo infrastructure/vps/firewall.sh
          sudo iptables -S DOCKER-USER
          sudo ip6tables -S DOCKER-USER
          [ "$(sudo iptables -S DOCKER-USER | grep -c DROP)" = 2 ]
          [ "$(sudo ip6tables -S DOCKER-USER | grep -c DROP)" = 2 ]

      - name: Sign in behind the server's proxy
        env:
          VIBLD_OWNER_PASSWORD: [REDACTED]
          VIBLD_DOMAIN: build.vibld.test
          VIBLD_PREVIEW_DOMAIN: vibld-preview.test
        run: |
          node docker/smoke.mjs 900
          # Through the proxy, as a browser would: https, the builder's own
          # origin, and a session cookie marked Secure.
          resolve='--resolve build.vibld.test:443:127.0.0.1 --resolve 8080-x-y.vibld-preview.test:443:127.0.0.1'
          curl --silent --show-error --insecure $resolve --dump-header headers.txt --output /dev/null \
            --request POST https://build.vibld.test/api/owner/session \
            --header 'content-type: application/json' --header 'origin: https://build.vibld.test' \
            --data "{\"password\":\"$VIBLD_OWNER_PASSWORD\"}"
          grep -i '^HTTP/.* 200' headers.txt
          grep -i '^set-cookie:.*; Secure' headers.txt > /dev/null
          echo 'the owner signs in through the proxy'
          # Any other host goes to the preview Worker, which knows no such
          # preview.
          status=$(curl --silent --insecure $resolve --output /dev/null --write-out '%{http_code}' https://8080-x-y.vibld-preview.test/)
          echo "an unknown preview answers $status"
          [ "$status" -ge 400 ] && [ "$status" -lt 500 ]
          # And nothing answers on the Workers' ports from outside the server.
          ip=$(hostname -I | awk '{ print $1 }')
          for port in 8787 8788 8789; do
            if curl --silent --max-time 5 "http://$ip:$port/" > /dev/null; then
              echo "a Worker answers on $ip:$port"; exit 1
            fi
          done
          echo "the Workers' ports are closed to $ip"
          # A client cannot pick its own address: wrong passwords, each with a
          # different forged CF-Connecting-IP, still run into the limit.
          # IP_BURST allows 20 a minute in fixed windows, so a run that
          # straddles a minute boundary can pass 40 before one is refused:
          # 45 attempts are refused in either case.
          limited=no
          for n in $(seq 1 45); do
            status=$(curl --silent --insecure $resolve --output /dev/null --write-out '%{http_code}' \
              --request POST https://build.vibld.test/api/owner/session \
              --header 'content-type: application/json' --header 'origin: https://build.vibld.test' \
              --header "cf-connecting-ip: 198.51.100.$n" --data '{"password":"wrong"}')
            if [ "$status" = 429 ]; then limited=yes; break; fi
          done
          [ "$limited" = yes ]
          echo "forged addresses are throttled after $n attempts"

      - name: Logs behind the server's proxy
        if: always()
        run: docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f infrastructure/vps/compose.yml logs --no-color | tail -n 300

  # The marketing template is deliberately outside the pnpm workspace: it has
  # to install and build on its own, with npm and no Vibld packages, because
  # that is what a user who exports it will do. Building it here is the only
  # way that claim stays true.
  template:
    name: Marketing template
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: templates/marketing
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: templates/marketing/package-lock.json

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      - name: Test
        run: npm test

      # A user who exports the template runs this next, so it has to work.
      - name: Build
        run: npm run build

  # The Luminous template sits outside the workspace for the same reason as
  # the marketing template: a user who exports it installs and builds it with
  # npm alone, so that is how CI builds it too.
  luminous-template:
    name: Luminous template
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: templates/luminous
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: templates/luminous/package-lock.json

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      - name: Test
        run: npm test

      # A user who exports the template runs this next, so it has to work.
      - name: Build
        run: npm run build

name: Deploy marketing preview

# Manual only, like the production deploy it shadows. This exists so a change
# to vibld.com can be looked at on a real Worker before it becomes the front
# door -- there was previously no way to see the marketing site anywhere but
# production.
on:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: deploy-marketing-preview
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  deploy:
    name: Build and deploy the marketing preview
    # Runs only in the private working repository. The public copy
    # (vibld/vibld) has none of the secrets or deployment environments this
    # job reads, so there it could only fail.
    if: github.repository == 'vibld/vibld-internal'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    # The build prerenders a page per gallery style (D143).
    timeout-minutes: 15

    # The same environment the production marketing deploy uses, so the
    # Cloudflare credentials are configured in one place. This job needs only
    # the two Cloudflare values: no Resend key is synced, deliberately.
    environment:
      name: marketing
      url: ${{ steps.deploy.outputs.url }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Require deploy credentials
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
        run: |
          missing=0
          [ -n "$CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" ] || { echo "::error::CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN is not set"; missing=1; }
          [ -n "$CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID" ] || { echo "::error::CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID is not set"; missing=1; }
          if [ "$missing" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "Add both to the \"marketing\" environment (Settings -> Environments)." >&2
            echo "This deploy needs only \"Workers Scripts: Edit\" -- unlike the production deploy, it creates no DNS records." >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Enable Corepack
        run: corepack enable

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build
        run: pnpm --filter @vibld/marketing build

      - name: Deploy the preview
        id: deploy
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/marketing
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          log="$RUNNER_TEMP/wrangler-preview.log"
          pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 deploy -c wrangler.preview.jsonc | tee "$log"

          # The workers.dev subdomain is account-specific, so the URL is not
          # knowable before the deploy. Wrangler prints it.
          url="$(grep -oE 'https://[a-z0-9.-]+\.workers\.dev' "$log" | head -n 1 || true)"
          if [ -z "$url" ]; then
            echo "::error::Deployed, but no workers.dev URL appeared in the output. Check that workers_dev is enabled for this account."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "url=$url" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Marketing preview: $url" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      # The point of this deploy is a URL a person can open, so a green upload
      # that answers nothing is not a success. The noindex check matters just
      # as much: this is a copy of vibld.com on a public hostname, and an
      # indexable copy would compete with the site it is previewing.
      #
      # The availability check retries, because the first version of this did
      # not and failed a perfectly good deploy: it asked 0.2 seconds after
      # wrangler returned and got a 404 from a workers.dev route that was not
      # serving yet. Failing on that teaches people to ignore this job, which
      # is exactly what must not happen to the noindex assertion below.
      #
      # The noindex check deliberately does not retry. Once the site answers,
      # a missing header is a real fault rather than a timing artefact.
      - name: Smoke test the preview
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          url="${{ steps.deploy.outputs.url }}"
          headers="$RUNNER_TEMP/headers.txt"

          status=000
          for attempt in $(seq 1 12); do
            status="$(curl -s -o /dev/null -D "$headers" -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 20 "$url/" || echo "000")"
            [ "$status" = "200" ] && break
            echo "attempt $attempt: $url/ answered $status, waiting for the route to serve"
            sleep 5
          done

          if [ "$status" != "200" ]; then
            echo "::error::$url/ still answered $status after about a minute. The upload succeeded, so this is the route not serving rather than a build problem."
            exit 1
          fi

          if ! grep -qi '^x-robots-tag:.*noindex' "$headers"; then
            echo "::error::$url/ is missing the noindex header. Refusing to call this preview ready: an indexable copy of vibld.com competes with the real site."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "$url/ is live and noindex." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

name: Deploy marketing site

# On every push to main that changes what vibld.com is built from, and by
# hand (Chris, D106). It was manual only, to avoid redeploying on unrelated
# merges; the paths below do that instead, and a manual-only deploy left
# vibld.com a day and a half behind main on 2026-09-30.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - apps/marketing/**
      # The site reads the style presets, the model catalogue, the template
      # catalog and the backgrounds from packages/ai, plans and prices from
      # these Worker modules (apps/marketing/turbo.json), and the examples.
      - packages/ai/**
      - packages/brand/**
      - packages/security-headers/**
      - apps/web/worker/entitlement.ts
      - apps/web/worker/signup-credit.ts
      - apps/web/worker/stripe-client.ts
      - apps/web/worker/referral.ts
      - apps/web/worker/model-access.ts
      - examples/**
      - pnpm-lock.yaml
      - .github/workflows/deploy-marketing.yml
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: deploy-marketing
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  deploy:
    name: Build and deploy vibld.com
    # Runs only in the private working repository. The public copy
    # (vibld/vibld) has none of the secrets or deployment environments this
    # job reads, so there it could only fail.
    if: github.repository == 'vibld/vibld-internal'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    # The build prerenders a page per gallery style (D143).
    timeout-minutes: 15

    # Credentials live on this environment rather than the repository, so
    # they are reachable only from a job that names it, and any protection
    # rule configured on it (a required reviewer) gates the run before a
    # single step executes.
    environment:
      name: marketing
      url: ${{ steps.deploy.outputs.url }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # Full history, so postbuild.ts can date each page in sitemap.xml
          # from the last commit that touched it. A shallow clone knows one
          # commit, and postbuild then leaves lastmod out rather than stamp
          # every page with the same date.
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Require deploy credentials
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
        run: |
          missing=0
          [ -n "$CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" ] || { echo "::error::CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN is not set"; missing=1; }
          [ -n "$CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID" ] || { echo "::error::CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID is not set"; missing=1; }
          if [ "$missing" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "Add both to the \"marketing\" environment (Settings -> Environments)." >&2
            echo "The Cloudflare token needs \"Workers Scripts: Edit\" and \"DNS: Edit\" on the vibld.com zone -- the routes in wrangler.jsonc create that zone's records on first deploy -- and \"D1: Edit\" on the account, for the roadmap's migrations." >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Enable Corepack
        run: corepack enable

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build
        run: pnpm --filter @vibld/marketing build

      # TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY is a Worker secret, not a build input, so it is
      # pushed separately from the deploy -- the same reasoning as the
      # model-key sync in deploy-web-preview.yml.
      #
      # It is optional: it is not in "Require deploy credentials" above, and
      # without it the roadmap (worker/roadmap.ts) refuses a browser's first
      # vote rather than the deploy failing (docs/decisions.md L29) -- so it
      # is synced only when present, the same `[ -n ... ]` pattern
      # deploy-web-preview.yml uses for the model keys.
      - name: Sync Worker secrets
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/marketing
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY: ${{ secrets.TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The value goes in on stdin so it never appears in a command line
          # or in the run log.
          if [ -n "$TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY" ]; then
            printf '%s' "$TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY" | pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 secret put TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY
            echo "Synced TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          else
            echo "TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY not set -- /roadmap refuses a browser's first vote on this deploy." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi

      # Idempotent -- wrangler tracks applied migrations in the database's own
      # `d1_migrations` table and only runs what is new. Runs before the
      # deploy itself so a Worker never goes live expecting a table a
      # migration this same push added hasn't created yet: the same step, for
      # the same reason, as deploy-web-preview.yml's for apps/web. The job's
      # `if: github.repository == 'vibld/vibld-internal'` guard covers it.
      - name: Apply D1 migrations
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/marketing
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
        run: pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 d1 migrations apply vibld-marketing-roadmap --remote

      - name: Deploy to Cloudflare Workers
        id: deploy
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/marketing
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
        run: |
          log="$RUNNER_TEMP/wrangler-deploy.log"
          pnpm dlx wrangler@4.137.0 deploy | tee "$log"
          url="$(grep -oE 'https://vibld\.com' "$log" | head -n 1 || true)"
          if [ -n "$url" ]; then
            echo "url=$url" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          echo "Deployed vibld-marketing (vibld.com, www.vibld.com)" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      # A green deploy only says the upload worked, not that the site is
      # answering. This used to warn and pass, for the days when a freshly
      # routed domain could still be propagating; vibld.com has been routed
      # since, so a site that does not answer is a failed deploy (internal PR 59).
      # A few tries, a few seconds apart, cover the edge picking up the new
      # version.
      - name: Smoke test the deployment
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          for attempt in 1 2 3 4 5; do
            status="$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 20 https://vibld.com/ || echo "000")"
            [ "$status" = "200" ] && break
            sleep 6
          done
          if [ "$status" != "200" ]; then
            echo "::error::https://vibld.com/ answered $status after five tries."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "https://vibld.com/ is live." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Notify IndexNow
        working-directory: apps/marketing
        run: pnpm indexnow

name: Deploy a generated preview

# Deploys a Vibld-generated project (ADR-0002: ordinary npm, no Vibld
# dependency) as its own Cloudflare Worker, purely so it can be viewed live --
# the builder shell's own preview pane only renders a local static mock and
# cannot run a model-generated project (sandbox execution is not implemented
# yet, ADR-0004). `directory` must already contain its own `wrangler.jsonc`
# naming a distinct Worker; this workflow does not invent one. Manual only.
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      directory:
        description: Path from the repo root to the generated project. Must contain its own wrangler.jsonc.
        required: true

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: deploy-preview-${{ github.event.inputs.directory }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  deploy:
    name: Build and deploy
    # Runs only in the private working repository. The public copy
    # (vibld/vibld) has none of the secrets or deployment environments this
    # job reads, so there it could only fail.
    if: github.repository == 'vibld/vibld-internal'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10

    # Reuses the same "preview" environment apps/web deploys to -- its
    # CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN already has Workers Scripts: Edit for the whole
    # account (apps/web/README.md explains why it can't be scoped tighter),
    # which covers deploying an additional, unrelated Worker too.
    environment:
      name: preview
      url: ${{ steps.deploy.outputs.url }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Require Cloudflare credentials
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
        run: |
          missing=0
          [ -n "$CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" ] || { echo "::error::CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN is not set"; missing=1; }
          [ -n "$CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID" ] || { echo "::error::CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID is not set"; missing=1; }
          if [ "$missing" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "Add both to the \"preview\" environment (Settings -> Environments)." >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Require the target directory and its wrangler.jsonc
        env:
          DIRECTORY: ${{ inputs.directory }}
        run: |
          if [ ! -f "$DIRECTORY/wrangler.jsonc" ]; then
            echo "::error::$DIRECTORY/wrangler.jsonc not found. This workflow deploys an existing generated project; it does not create one."
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 24

      # Plain npm, not pnpm: a generated project is deliberately not part of
      # the pnpm workspace, and is tested to build with ordinary npm commands.
      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.directory }}
        run: npm install --no-audit --no-fund

      - name: Build
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.directory }}
        run: npm run build

      - name: Deploy to Cloudflare Workers
        id: deploy
        shell: bash
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.directory }}
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
        run: |
          log="$RUNNER_TEMP/wrangler-deploy.log"
          npx wrangler@4.137.0 deploy | tee "$log"
          url="$(grep -oE 'https://[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.workers\.dev' "$log" | head -n 1 || true)"
          if [ -n "$url" ]; then
            echo "url=$url" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "Deployed to $url" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          else
            echo "::warning::Deploy succeeded but the URL could not be read from wrangler output"
          fi

# ADR-0003: Use provider adapters at external boundaries

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-09-06
- Decision owners: maintainers

## Context

Vibld will use changing external systems for AI models, sandboxes, source control, data, authentication, and deployment. Binding core orchestration or project models to a provider SDK would make replacement costly and undermine self-hosting.

## Decision

Core code defines capability-oriented contracts using Vibld-owned types. Provider integrations implement those contracts at the boundary. Provider SDK objects, errors, and configuration do not cross into core domain APIs. Adapters should expose real capability differences rather than pretending every provider is identical.

Create an abstraction only when at least one concrete workflow needs it; do not build a speculative universal plugin system during M1.

## Consequences

Providers can be tested and replaced independently and self-hosted deployments can choose their stack. Translation code and contract tests are required. Provider-specific capabilities may require explicit extensions or capability checks.

## Alternatives considered

- Direct SDK use throughout the codebase: faster for the first integration but expensive to unwind.
- A lowest-common-denominator interface: superficially portable but hides useful capabilities and failure modes.

# ADR-0004: Execute generated code as untrusted

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-09-06
- Decision owners: maintainers

## Context

Vibld installs dependencies and executes code assembled from model output and third-party packages. That code may be defective or malicious and cannot share the trust boundary of the Vibld control plane.

## Decision

All generated application commands run through a sandbox contract and are treated as untrusted. A sandbox receives only a project-scoped filesystem, explicit short-lived secrets, bounded resources, and policy-controlled network access. Vibld control-plane credentials are never available inside it. Lifecycle events and policy decisions are auditable.

The first sandbox implementation may support a narrow execution model, but the contract must preserve these invariants.

## Consequences

Preview and generation infrastructure require explicit isolation, timeouts, cleanup, and error reporting from the beginning. Local development may use a clearly labeled reduced-isolation adapter, but it cannot define the production security model.

## Alternatives considered

- Execute on the application host: operationally simple and unacceptable for hostile code.
- Rely only on static scanning: useful defense in depth, but unable to prove runtime safety.

# ADR-0006: Scoped authority and broker-first credentials

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-09-06
- Approval: D14(c), D15(a then b/c), D16(d), D17(b), D19(a)
- Refines: ADR-0004

## Context

Prompts, repositories, dependencies and generated applications are untrusted inputs. Broader autonomy must not grant those inputs access to platform credentials or other projects. Hosted previews run attacker-controlled JavaScript and must not share the builder's trust boundary.

## Decision

Represent grants outside model context with principal, tenant/project, actions, destination, budget and expiry. Check grants at each trusted tool boundary, including during retries. Deny actions outside the grant, and request a new user decision when scope changes. A standing grant avoids repeated prompts only within its approved scope. Revocation blocks new work; cancellation also stops active resources where possible.

| Credential class              | Allowed handling                                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Vibld infrastructure          | Trusted service bindings only; never sent to generated code                                                              |
| User model-provider key       | Encrypted at rest; used by trusted model service, with redaction and rotation                                            |
| GitHub authorization          | GitHub App installation access scoped to the intended repository and permissions; trusted Git operations                 |
| Deployment authorization      | Trusted deployment adapter scoped to approved target; production application secrets stored in the target's secret store |
| Generated-app test credential | Brokered operation first; narrowly scoped, expiring runtime injection only where required                                |

A broker authorizes operations, not arbitrary authenticated forwarding. Bind allowed methods, destinations and paths; validate redirects and block private-network/metadata destinations. Restrict response content and size. Never expose a generic proxy backed by broad credentials. Application test credentials remain separate from production secrets. A secret injected into untrusted runtime can be read by that runtime, so injection is a disclosed risk exception, not a guarantee against exfiltration.

Choose a user-secret store with separate encryption keys or a dedicated secret service before storing user keys. Specify key recovery, rotation, access audit and deletion. Do not place plaintext secrets in project objects, workflow payloads, Git, telemetry or model context. Exported apps use conventional environment configuration and can run with the user's direct credentials outside Vibld.

Apply filesystem, resource and outbound-network policy from the first hosted slice. Start with curated dependencies and explicit install destinations. Later broader install modes retain sandbox boundaries, execution caps and outbound policy. Reject path traversal, symlink escape and oversized file/command output before promotion or context assembly.

Preview access is private by default. Use an origin isolated from the builder, preferably a separate registrable domain, with no builder cookies or credentials. Authenticate HTML, assets and live connections; test that raw sandbox/port URLs cannot bypass access control. Validate parent/preview messages against exact origins and schemas. Sharing requires an explicit expiring grant, revocation and a warning about the exposed project content. Keep private previews out of shared caches and search indexing.

## Consequences

This adds trusted service code and integration tests to M1. Some integrations may not support usable narrow credentials; leave those unavailable until their risk is reviewed. Invitation-only access does not waive these controls. Refuse hosted alpha release if isolation, revocation or raw-URL bypass tests fail.

## Alternatives considered

- Inject every credential into the sandbox: simpler integration, unacceptable control-plane exposure.
- Broker every possible operation: useful default, but cannot support every conventional app integration.
- Grant broad autonomy as a prompt instruction: cannot enforce authorization or cost ceilings.
- Share public preview URLs by default: conflicts with the accepted private-preview requirement.

## References

- [Sandbox security](https://developers.cloudflare.com/sandbox/concepts/security/)
- [Sandbox outbound traffic](https://developers.cloudflare.com/sandbox/guides/outbound-traffic/)
- [GitHub installation access tokens](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/generating-an-installation-access-token-for-a-github-app)

/**
 * How many containers this deployment may have at once, and who gets them.
 *
 * `wrangler.jsonc` sets `max_instances` on the `PreviewSandbox` class, and
 * Cloudflare enforces it as a hard platform limit underneath
 * `PreviewFleet`'s own queue. Until internal PR 196 every container of that class was
 * a preview, so the platform limit and L9's preview cap were the same
 * number.
 *
 * Since internal PR 196 a build runs in an instance of the same class, named for
 * building, and holds one of the platform's containers while it does. Internal PR 196
 * split the budget statically to keep the fleet from admitting a preview
 * the platform had no room for: twenty for previews, five kept back for
 * builds, counted by two separate fleet instances. That was safe and it
 * broke L9, which reads "25 concurrent previews across all users. The 26th
 * request is queued with a visible position, not rejected." The
 * twenty-first preview queued whether or not anything was building.
 *
 * Chris chose the shared budget on 2026-09-27 (internal issue 197), and this is it:
 * previews and builds are counted against one budget of twenty-five, in one
 * `PreviewFleet` instance, with builds bounded at five of it. Previews get
 * all twenty-five whenever nothing is building, which meets L9 whenever a
 * twenty-five container budget can meet it, and a preview queues behind a
 * build only when every container is genuinely taken. A queued preview may
 * therefore be waiting for a build to finish rather than for another
 * preview, and its position still counts truthfully: builds never wait in
 * the queue (see `BUILD_MAX_IN_FLIGHT`), so everybody ahead of it is a
 * preview, and whichever kind of work frees a container, it goes to the
 * head of the queue.
 *
 * One counter rather than two is also what keeps the total honest. The
 * static split was counted on both sides only after a review round found
 * six builds overlapping nineteen previews with the fleet still believing
 * it had room; a single table that counts every container it has
 * authorised cannot be out of step with itself that way.
 *
 * The limits live here and the fleet reads them itself. Callers used to
 * pass their cap on every call, which was harmless while each instance
 * served one kind of caller. With both kinds sharing one instance, a
 * release that passed the wrong cap would promote the queue under it, so
 * no caller passes a cap any more.
 */

/** The one `PreviewFleet` instance, which counts previews and builds alike. */
export const FLEET_NAME = 'fleet';

/** What `wrangler.jsonc` gives the class. `capacity.test.ts` checks it. */
export const CONTAINER_MAX_INSTANCES = 25;

/**
 * How many containers the fleet authorises at once, previews and builds
 * together: the whole platform limit, and L9's twenty-five when nothing is
 * building.
 */
export const ACCOUNT_MAX_IN_FLIGHT = CONTAINER_MAX_INSTANCES;

/**
 * How many of those may be builds at once.
 *
 * Five rather than one because a build is not the only thing in flight at
 * its own moment: a repair builds twice, auto-publish builds again, and
 * several callers can be finishing runs at once. A bound inside the budget
 * rather than slots kept back beside it, so previews lose nothing to it
 * while nothing is building, and can never be left with fewer than twenty.
 *
 * A build over the bound, or one that finds every container taken, is
 * refused on the spot rather than queued. It has a paid Workflow waiting on
 * its answer, so waiting would spend that Workflow's timeout, and a build
 * row left waiting would sit in front of previews and could be promoted
 * later for a caller that was already told `busy`.
 *
 * Builds are short-lived, hold no exposed port, and destroy their container
 * as they finish rather than idling out the class's `sleepAfter`, so the
 * bound is about how many can run at once rather than how many ran
 * recently.
 */
export const BUILD_MAX_IN_FLIGHT = 5;

/**
 * How many containers a Free preview may never take (D158, Chris,
 * 2026-10-05), so Free use filling the fleet cannot queue paying accounts.
 * A Free preview starts only while this many would still be free after it;
 * paid previews and builds may use every one. Five of the twenty-five, the
 * figure Chris agreed to.
 */
export const PAID_PREVIEW_RESERVED = 5;

-- Model provider keys set from the admin panel (docs/decisions.md D127,
-- D131, D132).
--
-- One row per provider. The key itself is never stored: only its
-- AES-GCM encryption under VIBLD_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY, a Worker secret this
-- database never sees, with the provider bound in as associated data so a
-- row's ciphertext cannot be moved to another provider's row. `last4` is
-- the only part of the key anything shows.
--
-- A key here is used ahead of the Worker secret of the same name (D131);
-- removing it falls back to that secret.
CREATE TABLE provider_keys (
  provider TEXT PRIMARY KEY
    CHECK (provider IN ('anthropic', 'deepseek', 'openai')),
  ciphertext TEXT NOT NULL,
  iv TEXT NOT NULL,
  last4 TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_by TEXT NOT NULL
);

# The vibld brand

The direction is **Signal**: one vermilion signal on graphite and chalk. Chris
chose it on 2026-09-27 from the approved "Live Build" mockup, replacing
**Offset** (coral and ultramarine on newsprint, chosen 2026-09-16). Signal
kept Offset's mark, one chevron printed twice out of register, and changed
only its inks.

Everything below that can be checked is checked. The palette lives in
`packages/brand/src/palette.ts` and its tests recompute every contrast figure
quoted here using this repository's own checker (`@vibld/ai`'s
`contrastRatio`), the one already used on model output. A brand guide whose
numbers nothing recomputes is a brand guide that goes stale quietly.

## The inks

| Ink       | oklch                     | hex       | What it is                                         |
| --------- | ------------------------- | --------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Vermilion | `oklch(0.666 0.224 34.3)` | `#ff4a1c` | The ghost impression, and the fill                 |
| Graphite  | `oklch(0.191 0.009 264)`  | `#121418` | The text ink on light, the mark's stroke, the tile |
| Chalk     | `oklch(0.966 0.004 106)`  | `#f4f4f1` | The stock everything prints on                     |

Each oklch triple lands exactly on the mockup's hex through `oklchToHex`.

The rest of each theme:

| Token           | Light               | Dark                |
| --------------- | ------------------- | ------------------- |
| `paper`         | Chalk `#f4f4f1`     | `#0e0f11`           |
| `surface`       | `#ffffff`           | `#16181b`           |
| `surfaceStrong` | `#ecede8`           | `#1d2024`           |
| `ink`           | Graphite `#121418`  | `#eeeee9`           |
| `inkMuted`      | `#4a4f57`           | `#a9adb3`           |
| `accent`        | Vermilion `#ff4a1c` | Vermilion `#ff4a1c` |
| `onAccent`      | `#140a06`           | `#140a06`           |
| `accentInk`     | `#c2310d`           | `#ff8260`           |
| `markInk`       | Graphite `#121418`  | `#eeeee9`           |
| `markOffset`    | Vermilion           | Vermilion           |
| `markBlend`     | `multiply`          | `screen`            |

And what they measure, every one a pairing the palette test walks:

| Pairing                          | Light | Dark  |
| -------------------------------- | ----- | ----- |
| Body text on paper               | 16.73 | 16.48 |
| Body text on surface             | 18.44 | 15.28 |
| Body text on the raised surface  | 15.67 | 14.05 |
| Muted text on paper              | 7.48  | 8.51  |
| Muted text on surface            | 8.24  | 7.89  |
| Muted text on the raised surface | 7.01  | 7.25  |
| A link on paper                  | 5.10  | 7.87  |
| Text on a vermilion fill         | 5.81  | 5.81  |
| The mark's load-bearing stroke   | 16.73 | 16.48 |

## The rule that catches everybody

**Vermilion cannot carry text.** Against chalk it measures **3.05**. That
clears the large-text bar (3.0) by five hundredths and fails the normal-text
bar (4.5), which is the worst kind of number: it looks fine in a mockup and
fails the first time a heading wraps, a monitor runs bright or the heading
lands on the raised surface instead, where it measures 2.86 and fails both.
It is the most recognizable color in the system and the one nobody may set a
heading, a link or a label in, at any size.

The refusals that follow from it, all enforced by tests rather than by
convention:

- Vermilion text on chalk: 3.05. On the raised surface: 2.86. Use the accent
  ink, `#c2310d` (5.10) on light or `#ff8260` (7.87) on dark.
- White text on a vermilion fill: 3.36. Chalk: 3.05. Text on vermilion is
  always `#140a06` (5.81).
- The theme's own ink on a vermilion fill. It is graphite in light mode and
  looks safe, and in dark mode it is `#eeeee9` on a fill that does not change:
  2.89. Muted ink on vermilion is 2.45 in light mode already.
- The light link ink left unflipped on the dark ground: 3.41. The dark link
  ink leaked into the light theme: 2.21 on chalk.

**Every focus indicator takes the accent ink, never the accent.** Every one:
a control that replaces the global ring with its own border and halo has to
clear the same bar on its own, and the prompt input's override did not. An
alpha ramp of the accent does not help, it makes it worse: vermilion at 64%
and 16% composites to 2.17:1 and 1.21:1 on chalk (the previous coral managed
1.87:1 and 1.16:1).

**The focus ring takes the accent ink, never the accent.** A focus indicator
exists to be seen, which is the one job vermilion cannot be trusted with:
3.05 against chalk clears the 3:1 bar for a non-text indicator by a margin
no display keeps, and 2.86 against the raised surface does not clear it at
all. The accent ink measures 4.77 on the raised surface and more everywhere
else. Pointing the ring at the accent when the previous direction landed
quietly halved the contrast of every keyboard focus ring in the product.

`apps/marketing/test/palette-use.test.ts` reads the source and fails the build
if any of these appears. It was written because all three were already
shipped: the consent banner's "Allow" button set its text color to
`--color-accent-contrast`, a token that never existed, so the one control
every visitor sees had no text color at all.

## The mark

One chevron, printed twice, the second impression two units down and right in
a 32-unit box, the pair blended with `mix-blend-mode: multiply` on light and
`screen` on dark.

**Vermilion is always the ghost.** That is what makes it the color people
recognize: it is the one that does not change. The other impression is the
stroke the shape's legibility actually rests on, and it changes with the
ground:

| Ground          | Load-bearing ink | Ratio |
| --------------- | ---------------- | ----- |
| Chalk           | Graphite         | 16.73 |
| Dark            | `#eeeee9`        | 16.48 |
| A graphite tile | Chalk            | 16.73 |

A mark drawn in vermilion alone is not a mark to rely on: 3.05 on chalk
clears the 3:1 non-text bar by a hair and 2.86 on the raised surface does
not. `packages/brand/test/mark.test.ts` asserts the ghost never reads more
strongly than the ink.

**Anywhere the mark sits on a fixed ground, override the blend as well as the
inks.** The builder's logo tile is graphite whatever the page theme is, so it
sets `--vibld-mark-ink` to chalk, `--vibld-mark-offset` to vermilion and
`--vibld-mark-blend` to `screen`. Without the last one it would inherit
`multiply` in light mode and multiply a near-white stroke into graphite,
giving the ground back. That is exactly what the previous direction's
ultramarine tile shipped with. Overriding the two inks without the blend is
the shape of that mistake.

The tile is graphite because the favicon's is, so the tab and the header are
the same picture. In light mode it reads as a solid block (16.73 on chalk);
in dark mode it measures 1.04 against the ground and sinks into it, leaving
the mark as the dark theme draws it.

### When the overprint cannot survive

Named when the mark was first chosen: transparency is thrown away by
monochrome favicon rendering and by some email clients, leaving a muddy single
shape. `mark-mono.svg` is the answer. It draws the load-bearing ink only
(graphite), never the ghost, and it is generated rather than hand-drawn so it
cannot drift from the real mark.

## The wordmark

`vibld`, lowercase, everywhere: page titles, the header, the middle of a
sentence, legal copy. The capitalized form survives in exactly one place,
`SITE.legalName`, which feeds schema.org's `alternateName` so a search engine
can match the way people actually type it.

Set in Georgia, which is also the display face for headlines. There is no
webfont anywhere on the marketing site on purpose: the Cookie Notice
enumerates every third party the site contacts, and a font link would add one.

## The assets

All generated, none hand-drawn, by
`apps/marketing/scripts/brand-assets.ts`:

```
pnpm --filter @vibld/marketing brand:assets
```

- `favicon.svg`, the mark on a graphite tile: chalk stroke, vermilion ghost,
  `screen`
- `mark-mono.svg`, the single-ink fallback, in graphite
- `apple-touch-icon.png`, 180x180, the favicon's tile
- `favicon.ico`, the favicon's tile at 16, 32 and 48, for whatever asks for
  `/favicon.ico` by name
- `icon-192.png`, `icon-512.png` and `icon-maskable-512.png` (full bleed, the
  mark scaled into the safe zone), named by `manifest.webmanifest`
- `bimi.svg`, the logo mail providers show beside vibld.com mail (D173): SVG
  Tiny Portable/Secure, full bleed, the mark scaled into the middle for the
  circle crop. The test also checks the profile's rules.

  scale, the wordmark in chalk (16.73), the tagline in the dark link ink

manifest and fails if the committed files differ, so they cannot drift from
the palette. The icons and the manifest are written to app.vibld.com's
`apps/web/public/` too, and `apps/web/test/shell-brand.test.ts` checks both
hosts ship the same bytes.

**Never write `oklch()` into a file rendered outside a browser.** The first
social card the previous palette produced came out entirely black: librsvg,
which rasterises the PNGs, does not parse `oklch()` and falls back to black
rather than failing. Static assets use the `hex` field on each color, which
the palette test verifies against `oklchToHex`.

## Why one package

Before `@vibld/brand` existed, vibld.com shipped a warm orange chevron in
oklch and app.vibld.com shipped a purple-to-blue tilde in hsl. Two halves of
one product, two logos, two color systems, which is exactly what BRAND-01
(`docs/decisions.md`) forbids: searching "vibld" returns Bible-study sites, so
the only lever available is publishing one unambiguous entity everywhere.

Both apps now alias their existing token names onto `brand.css` rather than
declaring colors. That indirection is deliberate. It meant neither app had to
be rewritten to adopt the brand, it means there is exactly one place a color
is decided, and it is why moving from Offset to Signal changed no alias in
either app. Every theme token (`--vibld-paper`, `--vibld-accent`,
`--vibld-accent-ink` and the rest) kept its name and only its value moved;
the three named inks were renamed along with the inks themselves, to
`--vibld-vermilion`, `--vibld-graphite` and `--vibld-chalk`.

## First product acceptance scenario

An invited user requests a cybersecurity SaaS landing page with pricing, FAQ and a contact form. The builder explains its plan, generates a prerendered site, shows stage progress and presents a private working preview. A form without a backend must state that it is a demonstration.

The user can inspect changes and validation, save a checkpoint, reopen the project after sandbox eviction, and export a standalone project. With a scoped GitHub connection and approved destination, the user can create a branch and PR. Retrieval returns only the permitted project's current revision. Failure leaves the previous accepted checkpoint available and explains the failed stage without leaking secrets.

The follow-up request, "Make the hero simpler and reduce pricing from three plans to two," is the M2 conversational-edit acceptance scenario. The M1 bounded repair path provides groundwork but does not count as completing M2.

## Long-running generation streams

Generation outlives a normal request, and a stream that carries only model
output goes silent whenever the model is thinking. Browsers, mobile networks
and intermediate proxies drop an idle connection long before a job runtime's
own timeout, which surfaces to the user as a stream that "ended" with no error
and no failed stage.

Any transport that streams generation progress must therefore emit
transport-level keepalive events on its own schedule, independent of model
token activity, for as long as the run is active. Requirements:

- The keepalive interval is configuration, not a literal in route code, and has
  a documented default calibrated against the deployed edge and proxy timeouts.
  Do not assume a value carried over from an earlier system.
- Keepalives are driven by a timer over the whole run, not piggybacked on
  progress events, so a long planning phase before the first token still keeps
  the connection warm.
- Keepalive frames carry no project content, prompt text or credentials, and a
  client that ignores them must still parse the stream correctly.
- Stopping the keepalive is part of stream teardown on success, failure,
  cancellation and client disconnect; a leaked timer must not keep a run's
  resources alive.
- Reconnection and replay stay the mechanism for surviving a genuinely dropped
  connection. A keepalive reduces spurious drops; it does not replace durable
  run state (ADR-0007).

Cover an idle-model run, a client disconnect and a canceled run in the stream
tests.

## Release evidence

- Run a versioned prompt set covering different marketing layouts and content needs. Proposed initial target: ten prompts, three runs each, at least 27 of 30 successful within at most two repair attempts. Calibrate and record the gate before alpha admission; report uncertainty rather than generalizing from 30 runs.
- Report first-pass and post-repair success separately, along with first-preview time, cost per accepted result and the total cost of failures. Record provider/model/template versions and relevant run configuration.
- Every result counted as accepted passes an independent clean install, typecheck, build and run after export without Vibld services or `.vibld/`. Inspect route HTML, metadata, console failures, keyboard use and mobile layouts. Set performance/accessibility thresholds in the fixture specification; never use compiler success as a substitute.
- Inject invalid model output, install/build failure, timeout, cancellation, network loss, eviction, interrupted save, stale writer, stale index and ambiguous GitHub response. Verify bounded termination, conflict visibility, checkpoint recovery and deduplication.
- Prove cross-tenant denial across API, storage, retrieval, live status and previews. Test raw sandbox URL bypass, preview sharing expiry/revocation and credential redaction. A failing security invariant blocks release regardless of generation score.
- Test limits under concurrent requests and retries. Meter sandbox lifetime, token/tool usage, object retention and abandoned resources. Operator cleanup must not depend on a browser remaining connected.

# ADR-0001: Use a pnpm and Turborepo monorepo

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-09-06
- Decision owners: maintainers

## Context

Vibld will contain user-facing applications, orchestration logic, provider adapters, templates, and shared contracts that need coordinated changes. Publishing every conceptual boundary as an independent repository would add friction before those boundaries are proven.

## Decision

Use a single TypeScript repository with pnpm workspaces and Turborepo task orchestration. Product applications live under `apps/`; reusable, independently testable capabilities may graduate into `packages/`. A directory in the blueprint is not automatically a package.

## Consequences

Cross-cutting changes remain atomic, dependency installation is deduplicated, and validation has one entry point. The repository must actively prevent accidental coupling with package APIs, dependency direction, and tests. Turborepo is build tooling and must not become an application runtime dependency.

## Alternatives considered

- Multiple repositories: stronger isolation, but excessive coordination for Phase 0.
- A single application package: simpler initially, but obscures the known platform boundaries.
- npm or Yarn workspaces: viable, but pnpm offers strict, efficient dependency handling and matches the chosen contributor workflow.

# ADR-0002: Preserve generated-application portability

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-09-06
- Decision owners: maintainers

## Context

AI builders can create durable platform lock-in when exported applications depend on proprietary runtimes, opaque metadata, or hosted services merely to function.

## Decision

Generated applications are conventional standalone projects. They may include optional `.vibld/` metadata and `VIBLD.md`, but neither may contain application logic required at build time or runtime. Removing Vibld metadata must not break install, development, build, test, or deployment workflows.

The initial generated-app standard is React, TypeScript, and Vite, with familiar package scripts and documented environment variables. Vibld-specific runtime dependencies require a separate ADR.

## Consequences

Users can leave Vibld without rewriting their applications, standard developer tools continue to work, and templates require disciplined versioning. Some deeply integrated features may require generated conventional code instead of a convenient proprietary runtime.

## Alternatives considered

- A required Vibld runtime: accelerates platform features but violates the ownership promise.
- Export-time conversion: makes the in-product project differ from the exported artifact and creates a fragile escape path.
